findings.summary: D9 / acceptance criterion 9 is non-discriminating: the only content-clue cap test stubs `proposeContentClue` to return null and asserts that ingestMaterial forwards null, which merely re-states the stub. The real cap lives in the production assembly (`if (bc.value >= maxClues) return Promise.resolve(null)`), and no test drives it — every harvest unit test builds HarvestDeps without an `ingestMaterial` dep (test/harvest.test.ts:252-264), so deleting the production cap check leaves the whole suite green. The spec requires 'bypass the cap ⇒ test turns red'.

D9 / acceptance criterion 9 also requires the cap event to be observably reported, isomorphic to the existing clue cap (`skippedClues`). A content-clue suppressed by maxClues returns null from `ingestMaterial`, which harvest cannot distinguish from the D2 reuse path — both are silently dropped by `if (clue) {...}`. HarvestReport has `contentCluesPublished`/`contentCluesBlocked` but no counterpart to `skippedClues`, so a capped content-clue is a silent truncation.

Acceptance criterion 4 (D3 discriminative) is not met: no test anywhere asserts that a material produces a `doc(transcript)` on `research:content` with `doc_kind==="transcript"` and `origin` = the source URI. The single production-path test that carries a material (`runChannelWrite`) lands on the failure branch — the stubbed global fetch has no `arrayBuffer`, so `fetchMaterialHttp` throws and the assertions are `contentCluesBlocked===1`. The whole successful ingest path (fetch → authoritative digest → publishDoc) is never exercised through the assembled deps.

The second half of acceptance criterion 4 is missing entirely: there is no regression test for `materials: []` ⇒ ingest called zero times and bus write count byte-identical to base. `harvestDeps()` never provides an `ingestMaterial` stub, so no test can count ingest invocations at all; the empty-materials path is only incidentally covered by unrelated E2b evidence tests.

Acceptance criteria 2/3/6/7 (D1/D2/D4/D5 discriminative) are asserted only against hand-written `IngestDeps` literals in the unit test, never against the production-assembled deps. The assembly that wires `readExistingTranscript` to `research:content`, `transcribe` to MinerU `fileParse`, and `publishDoc` to the content channel has zero test coverage; a mis-wire there (e.g. reading the board instead of the content channel) would not turn any test red. Criterion 10 explicitly requires assertions on the production-assembled deps and forbids bypassing the assembly chain.

D7 / acceptance criterion 8 is asserted on `ingestBatch`, which has no production caller (grep of src shows it referenced only by its own definition and the test). The production path calls `ingestMaterialImpl` once per material with the `serialize` argument omitted, so each material gets a fresh `createMutex()`; in-flight===1 holds only because harvest's for-loop awaits sequentially, not because of the shared mutex the test exercises. The starred concurrency assertion therefore does not cover the shipped code path.

`publishDoc` (content channel) and `publishClue` (board channel) reuse the identical idempotency key `dr-content:<run_id>:<i>` for two different messages of two different kinds. This is safe only if the bus scopes idempotency keys per channel; that assumption is undocumented and untested here.

The first test in the ingest suite asserts module properties by reading src/ingest.ts with readFileSync and regex-matching its text. Criterion 10 states that source-string matching does not constitute evidence; this test is inherited rather than new, but it should not be counted toward any E1 criterion.

Non-blocking positives confirmed by reading the product code: D1 order is fetch → compute sha256 → dedup lookup with the worker-reported digest fully ignored as a key; D2 returns the existing doc without touching MinerU; D4 builds the clue with sources:["content"], parent = original clue id, depth = parent depth (not +1) and text carrying digest + origin; D5 skips propose on the reuse path; D6 sinks failure to the material (no markBlocked of the parent, no rethrow, parent still CAS-ed to explored and its evidence still published); CLUE_TRANSITIONS was not loosened; D8 fetchMaterialHttp fails loudly on non-2xx, zero bytes and >4MB. The rejection is about missing/circular acceptance evidence, not about these behaviours. Criterion 1 (npm ci / typecheck / test twice green) and criteria 13-14 (live-machine) could not be checked by this read-only review.
